zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Maʿārij
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَألَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ﴾ ("A questioner asked for a punishment bound to fall"). It was also read «سالَ» without hamza. One says «سَألْتُ، أسْألُ» and «سَلْتُ، أسالُ», and «الرَّجُلانِ يَتَساءَلانِ» and «يَتَساوَلانِ» ("the two men ask each other") with one meaning. The interpretation is: "A caller called for a punishment bound to fall", and that is like their saying: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ أوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32] ("O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"). It was also said that the meaning of «سَألَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ» is: [he asked] about a punishment bound to fall, and the answer is His saying: ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دافِعٌ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 2] ("for the unbelievers; there is none to avert it"), i.e. it will fall upon the unbelievers. And it was said that in «سالَ سايِلٌ» without hamza, «سايِل» is a valley in Hell.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَلا يَسْألُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا﴾ ("And no close friend will ask about a close friend"). It was also read «وَلا يُسْألُ حَمِيمٌ» ("no close friend will be asked [about]"). Whoever reads «وَلا يَسْألُ», the meaning is that they recognise one another, and what indicates it is His saying ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 11] ("they will be shown them"). Whoever reads «وَلا يُسْألُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا», the meaning is: "No relative will be asked about his kin", and ﴿يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 11] — and Allah knows best — would refer to the angels.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَفَصِيلَتِهِ الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ﴾ ("and his clan that sheltered him") means: the nearest of his tribe to him.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا إنَّها لَظى﴾ ("No! Indeed, it is Laẓā"): «كَلّا» is a deterrent and a warning, i.e. "None of these will return, so take heed."

zajjaj:16-16.t:
It was read ﴿نَـزّاعَةً لِلشَّوى﴾ ("plucking off the extremities", accusative), while the [established] reading is «نَزّاعَةٌ» (nominative), and the readers follow it; in grammar it is stronger than the accusative. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned that it [the accusative] is permissible in Arabic, and that he did not know anyone who read it so. It has been narrated from al-Ḥasan, and there is disagreement about it from ʿĀṣim: what Abū ʿAmr narrated from ʿĀṣim is ﴿نَـزّاعَةً﴾ in the accusative, while others narrated «نَزّاعَةٌ» in the nominative.
As for the nominative, it is from three angles. One of them is that «لَظى» and «نَزّاعَة» are both the khabar (predicate) of the hāʾ and alif [of «إنَّها»], as you say «إنَّهُ حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ» ("it is sweet-sour"), meaning that it combines both tastes; the hāʾ and alif would then be a pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa) — what the Kufans call "the unknown (al-majhūl)" — and the meaning is: "the story and the matter is: Laẓā, plucking off the extremities." «الشَّوى» are the extremities: the two hands, the two feet and the head; and «الشَّوى» is the plural of «شَواة», which is the skin of the head. The poet said:
؎قالَتْ قُتَيْلَةُ ما لَهُ ∗∗∗ قَدْ جُلِّلَتْ شَيْبًا شَواتُهْ؟
(Qutayla said: What is the matter with him, his scalp all covered in grey?)
As for the accusative of ﴿نَـزّاعَةً﴾, it is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of emphasis (ḥāl muʾakkida), as He said: ﴿وَهُوَ الحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 91] ("while it is the truth, confirming"), and as you say «أنا زَيْدٌ مَعْرُوفًا» ("I am Zayd, well known"); so ﴿نَـزّاعَةً﴾ is accusative, emphasising the matter of the Fire. It may also be accusative on the meaning that it blazes (tatalaẓẓā) as one that plucks off, as He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ [al-Layl: 14] ("So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes"). The third angle for the nominative: it is nominative as [an expression of] censure (dhamm), with an implied «هِيَ», in the sense: "it is one that plucks off the extremities." Its accusative may also be as censure, so its accusative is on three angles.
[Translator's note: the text announces three angles for the nominative but, between the first and the "third", gives the accusative analyses; the second nominative angle is not stated explicitly. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿تَدْعُو مَن أدْبَرَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ("It calls whoever turned his back and went away"): it calls the unbeliever by his name and the hypocrite by his name.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا﴾ ("Indeed, man was created anxious"): «الهَلُوع», according to the explanation contained in the verse [itself], is one who is frightened and impatient at evil.

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿إذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعًا﴾ ﴿وَإذا مَسَّهُ الخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 21] ("When evil touches him, impatient; and when good touches him, withholding"). «الإنْسان» here has the meaning of "people", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made an exception of the believers who pray, saying: ﴿إلا المُصَلِّينَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 22] ﴿الَّذِينَ هم عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ دائِمُونَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 23] ("except those who pray, who are constant in their prayer"): He means by it those who keep up the prescribed prayer. It is also possible that it means "those who do not turn their faces away from the direction of the qibla and do not look around", so that its derivation would be from «الدّائِم», which is the still — as the prohibition has come against urinating in still (dāʾim) water. And «المَحْرُوم» ("the deprived") is the one who is luckless, who has been deprived of earnings and does not ask.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ﴾ ﴿إلا عَلى أزْواجِهِمْ أوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهم فَإنَّهم غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 30] ("And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for they are not to be blamed"), i.e. with respect to these. It was said that it [«عَلى»] has the meaning of «مِن»; the meaning according to the one who says this is: "except from their wives or those their right hands possess". And it was said that «عَلى» is construed according to the sense, the meaning being: "for they are not blamed regarding their wives", and what indicates this is ﴿فَإنَّهم غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 30].

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿ذِي المَعارِجِ﴾ ("Owner of the ways of ascent"): it was said: "the ascending stairways of the angels"; and it was said: "Owner of the [heavenly] bounties (fawāḍil)".
[Translator's note: the source prints «ذِي الفَواصِلِ»; the usual gloss is «ذِي الفَواضِلِ» ("Owner of bounties"), so this is probably a misprint. Translated in that sense.]

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ﴾ ("then those are the transgressors"): its meaning is in [the sense of] ʿudwān (aggression), which is going to extremes in opposing Allah's command and exceeding the measure in wrongdoing. And it was said: ﴿فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وراءَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ﴾ ("So whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors"), i.e. whoever seeks other than wives and those whom the right hands possess has transgressed. «العادُون» is the plural of «عادٍ», [plural] «عادُونَ».

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لأماناتِهِمْ وعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ﴾ ("And those who are keepers of their trusts and their covenant"), i.e. they observe the covenant and the trust and safeguard them. Everyone who safeguards something is an observer (murāʿin) of it, and the leader is a shepherd (rāʿin) of his flock.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَمالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ("So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, hastening towards you with fixed gaze?"): «مُهْطِعِينَ» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «المُهْطِع» is one who directs his gaze at a thing and does not leave it, because they used to look at the Prophet (peace be upon him) with a look of enmity. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَتَراهم يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ وهم لا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 198] ("And you see them looking at you while they do not see"); its meaning is: [looking] in rage and resentment.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿عَنِ اليَمِينِ وعَنِ الشِّمالِ عِزِينَ﴾ ("on the right and on the left, in separate groups"): circle by circle, group by group. «عِزِينَ» is the plural of «عِزَة». They were gathered on his right and his left, and they said: "If Muḥammad's companions enter Paradise, we shall enter it before them, and if they are given something in it, we shall be given more than that." So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنهم أنْ يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 38] ("Does every man among them aspire to be admitted to a Garden of bliss?"); it was also read «أنْ يَدْخُلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ» ("to enter a Garden of bliss"). Then He said: ﴿كَلا إنّا خَلَقْناهم مِمّا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 39] ("No! Indeed, We created them from what they know"), i.e. from dust and from a drop of sperm — so what do they have by which they would be admitted to Paradise, while they persist in enmity and hatred towards you?!

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿تَعْرُجُ المَلائِكَةُ والرُّوحُ إلَيْهِ في يَوْمٍ كانَ مِقْدارُهُ خَمْسِينَ ألْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾ ("The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years"). It has come in the exegesis that it is the Day of Resurrection; and it has also come that its measure, were you to undertake it, would be fifty thousand years, whereas the angels ascend in every single day. It was read «تَعْرُجُ المَلائِكَةُ» and «يَعْرُجُ المَلائِكَةُ». It was also said: from the first of the days of this world until its end is fifty thousand years. And it is possible that «فِي يَوْمٍ» belongs to (is attached to) «واقِعٍ», so the meaning would be: "A questioner asked for a punishment bound to fall on a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years", and that punishment falls on the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:40-41.t: His saying: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ المَشارِقِ والمَغارِبِ إنّا لَقادِرُونَ﴾ ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ خَيْرًا مِنهُمْ﴾ ("So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that We are able to replace them with better than them"). Its meaning is: "So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests", and «لا» is emphatic, as He said: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29], whose meaning is "so that the People of the Book may know". The meaning of ﴿بِرَبِّ المَشارِقِ والمَغارِبِ﴾ is: the rising-places of the sun and its setting-places, and likewise of the moon; these are the rising-places of summer and of winter and the setting-places of summer and of winter. The sun rises each day from a [different] rising-place and sets in a [different] setting-place, and likewise the moon.

zajjaj:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿فَذَرْهم يَخُوضُوا ويَلْعَبُوا حَتّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾ ("So leave them to indulge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised"): «يَخُوضُوا» is the answer to the imperative, jussive (majzūm). It was also said that it is jussive, even though its wording lacks the particle of command, because it was put in the place of the imperative, as if He said: «لِيَخُوضُوا ولِيَلْعَبُوا» ("let them indulge and let them play"). This is a command by way of threat, as you say: "Do what you like, for I shall punish you for it." The explanation of this has already been given exhaustively.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ سِراعًا كَأنَّهم إلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ﴾ ("The Day they will come out of the graves rapidly, as if racing to a nuṣub"). «الأجْداث» are the graves; their singular is «جَدَث», and «جَدَف» is also said with this meaning. It was read «إلى نَصْبٍ يُوفِضُونَ» and «إلى نُصْبٍ» with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, and it was read ﴿إلى نُصُبٍ﴾ with ḍamma on the nūn and the ṣād. Whoever reads «نَصْبٍ», its meaning is: "as if [racing] to a marker set up (manṣūb) for them…"; and whoever reads «إلى نُصْبٍ», its meaning is: "to idols of theirs…", as He said: ﴿وَما ذُبِحَ عَلى النُّصُبِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 3] ("and what is slaughtered on stone altars"). The meaning of ﴿يُوفِضُونَ﴾ is: they hasten. The poet said:
؎لَأنْعَتَنَّ نَعامَةً مِيفاضًا ∗∗∗ خَرْجاءَ تَغْدُو وتَطْلُبُ الأضّاضا
(I shall surely describe a swift ostrich, pied black and white, running off at dawn and seeking a refuge.)
«المِيفاض» is the swift one; «خَرْجاء» is one of two colours, black and white; and the meaning of «الأضّاض» is the place in which refuge is sought; one says «أضَتْنِي إلَيْكَ الحاجَةُ أضاضًا» ("need has driven me to you").

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿تَرْهَقُهم ذِلَّةٌ﴾ ("abasement will cover them"), i.e. abasement will overspread them.
And His saying: ﴿مِن عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 11] ("from the punishment of that Day") was read with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads «يَوْمِ» with kasra does so on the basic rule of annexation (iḍāfa), because the word to which the first is annexed is genitive (majrūr) by annexation. Whoever reads «يَوْمَ» with fatḥa does so because it is annexed to something non-declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) — annexed to «إذْ», and «إذْ» is vague (mubhama); its meaning is "the day when such-and-such happens". Since it is vague and [the noun] is annexed to it, the word annexed to it was made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. In the same way they recited the poet's saying:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing prevented her from drinking except that a dove cooed among branches laden with fruit.)
When he annexed «غَيْرَ» to «أنْ», he made it indeclinable on fatḥa, though it is in the position of a nominative. The nominative has also been narrated: they said «غَيْرُ أنْ نَطَقَتْ», just as the word [in the verse] was read with the genitive inflection and with indeclinability on fatḥa.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فاصْبِرْ صَبْرًا جَمِيلا﴾ ("So be patient with a beautiful patience"): this indicates that it was before the Prophet (peace be upon him) was commanded to fight.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّهم يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا﴾ ﴿وَنَراهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 7] ("Indeed, they see it as far off, but We see it as near"): they see it as far off in their view, as though they consider it remote in the sense of [its being] impossible, just as you say to your opponent in debate: "This is far-fetched; it cannot be."

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿وَنَراهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ ("but We see it as near"), i.e. sound, its like being easy to understand through the way Allah has given evidence for the Day of Raising by His saying ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79] ("Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time"), and similar arguments concerning the raising.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ كالمُهْلِ﴾ ﴿وَتَكُونُ الجِبالُ كالعِهْنِ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 9] ("The Day the sky will be like muhl, and the mountains like ʿihn"): «العِهْن» is wool, and «المُهْل» is the dregs of oil.
